text.p: - The Slovenian government on Thursday extended asylum for Bosnian refugees until the end of July. There are still over 8,300 Bosnian refugees in Slovenia.

- Turkish President Suleyman Demirel started his two-day visit to Slovenia on Thursday with a meeting with President Milan Kucan. Demirel said Turkey would support Slovenia's efforts to join NATO and the European Union.
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek visited his Swedish colleague Goeran Persson on Thursday. The two prime ministers discussed mutual relations and Slovenia's bid for EU and NATO membership.
- Supreme commander of NATO Europe George Joulwan ending a two-day visit to Slovenia thanked the state for its contribution to NATO Stabilisation Force operations in Bosnia.

- A group of Christian Democrat senior officials on Thursday demanded the resignation of the party leadership over its defeat in a November parliamentary election, in which the party got 10 out of 90 seats, down from 16 the previous term.

- Slovenia's Smelt Olimpija qualified for the Final Four in Rome after beating Italian Milan by 61-77 in the quarter-final third leg deciding match in the EuroLeague basketball championship on Thursday.

- A referendum will be held on whether to restitute large forest estates seized after World War II to their previous owners, after the leftist United List of Social Democrats managed to get over 40,000 signatures in favour of a referendum.

- Over 42 percent of Slovenians questioned support the country's bid for full NATO membership, 28 percent are opposed, while the rest were either undecided or had no opinion about the issue, an opinion poll by daily Dnevnik showed.
- Slovenian producer prices in March eased 0.5 percent compared to the previous month and rose five percent compared to March 1996, the Statistical Office reported on Thursday.
- A 1.5 percent cut in bank deposit interest rates from the beginning of April did not significantly hurt large-scale investors, analysts said.
- The total turnover on the Ljubljana bourse fell in March to eight billion tolars ($52.4 million), down from 30 billion in February, the bourse said.
